test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 29th November 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The cost of 6 flats was ₹60 lakh each. A builder sold one-third of the flats at 15% profit and one-sixth of the flats at 6% loss. If he incurred a net loss of 10% after selling the remaining flats, what was his loss percentage in the remaining flats?
solution:
**Given:**

The cost of 6 flats was Rs 60 lakh each.

A builder sold one-third of the flats at a 15% profit and one-sixth of the flats at a 6% loss.

Formula Used:

Loss percentage = loss/CP × 100

Profit percentage = Profit /CP × 100

Profit = SP - CP and Loss = CP - SP where,

SP = Selling price and CP = Cost price.

**Concept used:**

Profit and Loss always calculated on cost price.

**Calculation:**

The total numbers of flats are 6

Remaining flats = 6 - (2 + 1)

⇒ 3

The total cost price of 6 flats = Rs 60 lakh × 6

⇒ 360 lakhs

He sold 1/3 of 6 = 2 flats at 15 % profit

So the selling price of those 2 flats will be 

2× 60 × (115 / 100) 

⇒ 138 lakhs

He sold 1 flat at 6% loss

So, the selling price of this flat will be 60 × (94 / 100) = 56.40 lakh

Total selling price of 6 flats = 360 × (90 / 100)

⇒ 324 lakh

The selling price of the remaining 3 flats = 324 - (138 + 56.40)

⇒ 129.6

Cost price of these 3 flats = Rs 60 lakh × 3 = 180 lakh

Total loss = 50.4 lakh

Loss percentage = (50.4 / 180) × 100

⇒ 28%

**∴ His loss percentage in the remaining flats was 28%.**
